notes.text: The sheet is a typed letter headed Massy le 3.11.1970 and addressed Cher Verdier, ending Bien cordialement without a visible signature. The lower-left 15 is archival and is kept as a comment. H’s double-carbon/author description is editorial, not source wording.
notes.basis: Observation: date, salutation, closing, and lower-left margin; no attribution beyond the supplied editorial description is asserted.

notes.text: The writer says he has scarcely worked on Math for three months and recalls outstanding SGA 4 material. The list visibly cancels IV, par.9 et suivants, retains V alone, and retains VI par.5 et suivants. The cancelled row’s comma and digit 9 were confirmed in crop 01.
notes.basis: Source assertions and recollection: opening paragraph and three-row list; crop 01 is a transcription inspection, not a proof check.

notes.text: The second Si je me rappelle bien introduces a recollection that the overtyped reference had been drafted and needed changes discussed before the recipient’s departure. The reference components remain uncertain in order and are not chosen from expected mathematical content.
notes.basis: Source wording: paragraph 2 first three lines; observed overtyping in crop 02. No contextual reconstruction.

notes.text: The writer thinks the recipient has Saint Donat’s VI B, says he is sending the same author’s Appendix to XVII, and says he had apparently read its first pages. He requests its return to himself or St Donat with annotations and comments.
notes.basis: Source statements and explicit qualifications je pense and apparemment: paragraph 2 around the separate VI B line.

notes.text: The writer presumes the recipient has a copy of XVII. He states that XVIII was typed directly on paper for offset rather than on Stencils, that typing is finished, and that Deligne is supposed to correct it. These are claims made by the letter, not independently verified production facts.
notes.basis: Source wording: paragraph 3, including Tu dois avoir and est censé.

notes.text: The last paragraph requests progress on writing and on reading VI B, expresses a wish for V, VI and VI with lowered B within two or three months, and asks whether and when the recipient intends to finish. Pourrais tu has no hyphen, Ecris-moi has an unaccented initial E, and en tous cas is visibly plural.
notes.basis: Observation of wording and punctuation in halves a/b; crop 04 confirms the blank between Pourrais and tu.

notes.text: The il after rédigé, is darker than adjacent type. Crop 03 does not isolate a distinct earlier character or a sufficiently clear displaced duplicate contour, so ordinary il is retained. At la frappe, by contrast, displaced same-letter contours are visible for both letters. The left-edge vertical mark beside paragraph 4 continues as a paper crease and is not read as a marginal annotation.
notes.basis: Direct observations: crops 03 and 06, and full/half-a margin inspection; no linguistic or mathematical repair.

notes.text: No mathematical checking was performed. The sheet reports correspondence, recollections, and editorial progress; transcription inspection is not entered as a mathematical check event. Normal spaces after abbreviations, line wrapping, and editorial macros in H are not counted as textual differences.
notes.basis: Scope of this reader run; check_events intentionally empty.
